title: The Strongest Animal on Earth Pulls 1,141 Times Its Own Weight

scenes.text: The strongest animal on Earth can pull 1,141 times its own weight.
It's a dung beetle. The size of a fingernail.
For you, that would be dragging 80 tonnes. Six double decker buses. Full.
Scientists measured it by hooking a thread to a male and pulling him out of his tunnel.
Why so strong? Males fight head to head in tunnels, for a female. The loser gets shoved out.
Strongest animal on the planet, for the weight. And it lives in poo.
scenes.keywords: dung beetle rolling dung ball savanna

description:
The dung beetle Onthophagus taurus can pull 1,141 times its own body weight, making it the strongest animal on Earth relative to size.
Researchers at Queen Mary University of London and the University of Western Australia measured the force needed to drag males out of their tunnels after a fight. Scaled to a 70 kilogram person, that pull would be about 80 tonnes, roughly six full double-decker buses. The strength evolved for head-to-head shoving matches between males inside the tunnels where females live.
What's the heaviest thing you've ever lifted? Comment below.
first_comment: Dung beetles also navigate by the Milky Way, the only insects known to steer by the stars. Strongest or best navigator: which superpower would you take?
